caption: What if you were a cheetah for a day? You'd wake up early, because unlike most cats, cheetahs hunt by day, mostly in the morning and late afternoon. Top speed is often quoted at about 100 km/h, and scientists tracking wild cheetahs in Botswana measured runs up to 93 km/h. The real weapon is acceleration: a single stride can add about 10 km/h, and each stride covers up to 7 metres. Blunt claws grip like running spikes, the long tail steers like a rudder, and the black tear marks may cut sun glare. But the average chase is only about 173 metres, and cheetahs lose roughly 1 in 10 kills to lions and hyenas. They can't roar either; they purr and chirp. India lost its cheetahs by 1952, and in 2022 eight arrived at Kuno from Namibia. Twist: cheetahs are so genetically alike that skin grafts between unrelated cheetahs were all accepted. Would YOU trade a roar for speed? 👇
